claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT analysis using the Stoner criterion can reliably predict ferromagnetic ground states.
The Stoner criterion is satisfied when N(E_F) multiplied by the Stoner exchange parameter I exceeds unity.
Satisfying the Stoner criterion causes exchange interactions to favor a spin-split ferromagnetic state.
Spin-polarized and non-spin-polarized DFT total energies can be compared to assess magnetic-state stability.
The density of states at the Fermi level and the Stoner parameter can be determined or estimated computationally.
The proposed calculations represent zero-temperature or static-lattice conditions without an external magnetic field.
A high density of states at the Fermi level is important for satisfying the Stoner criterion.
When N(E_F)·I exceeds one, exchange-energy gain from spin alignment overcomes the associated kinetic-energy cost.
Overcoming the kinetic-energy cost with exchange-energy gain stabilizes a ferromagnetic spin-split ground state.
Materials with N(E_F)·I greater than one will have a lower spin-polarized DFT total energy than their non-magnetic counterparts.
Materials with N(E_F)·I greater than one will have a finite calculated magnetic moment.
The predictive accuracy depends on the exchange-correlation functional and treatment of electron correlations.
Neglecting thermal effects can limit predictive accuracy.
The method is most reliable for systems in which the adopted DFT approximations are adequate.
The effective numerical threshold and computed values of N(E_F) and I may vary with the material and computational parameters.
Experimental verification is required to confirm the computational prediction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism present N(E_F)·I > 1 as a definite threshold, whereas the uncertainty field says the exact numerical threshold may vary. This is an unresolved qualification of the stated decision rule.
